_comment: Structured SQL Server -> Snowflake DDL conversion rules. This file is the source of truth for all mappings. The engine (converter.py) must consult this file rather than relying on model/LLM knowledge for any mapping decision.

type_mappings._comment: key = SQL Server base type (uppercase, no brackets/args). value.target = Snowflake type name. value.carry_args = whether (n) / (p,s) args are copied through unchanged. value.fixed_args = literal args to force (overrides carry_args). value.review = if present, always flag manual review with this reason even though a mapping exists.

TINYINT.review: SQL Server TINYINT is unsigned 0-255; Snowflake has no unsigned types. Mapped to SMALLINT - add a CHECK(col BETWEEN 0 AND 255) manually if the 0-255 range must be enforced.

TEXT.review: TEXT is deprecated in SQL Server. Mapped to Snowflake's max VARCHAR size (16MB); confirm this is large enough / actually needed.

NTEXT.review: NTEXT is deprecated in SQL Server. Mapped to Snowflake's max VARCHAR size (16MB); confirm this is large enough / actually needed.

BOOL.review: Some dialects (e.g. MySQL) use TINYINT(1) for BOOLEAN; ensure 0/1 values are interpreted as FALSE/TRUE when migrating.

NUMBER.review: Oracle/HANA NUMBER -> Snowflake NUMBER; preserve precision/scale when present.

VARCHAR2.review: Oracle VARCHAR2 -> Snowflake VARCHAR mapping; preserve length if provided.

SERIAL.review: Postgres SERIAL is a sequence-backed integer; map to INTEGER and convert autoincrement semantics to Snowflake AUTOINCREMENT where appropriate.

DATETIMEOFFSET.review: DATETIMEOFFSET stores an explicit UTC offset per row. Snowflake TIMESTAMP_TZ stores an offset too but display/session-timezone behavior differs - verify downstream consumers.

MONEY.review: MONEY has no exact Snowflake equivalent; mapped to NUMBER(19,4) which matches SQL Server MONEY precision/scale. Confirm rounding behavior at the application layer.

SMALLMONEY.review: SMALLMONEY has no exact Snowflake equivalent; mapped to NUMBER(10,4) which matches SQL Server SMALLMONEY precision/scale.

REAL.review: REAL (32-bit) and Snowflake FLOAT (64-bit double) have different precision. Confirm precision loss/gain is acceptable.

UNIQUEIDENTIFIER.review: No native UUID/GUID type in Snowflake. Mapped to VARCHAR(36) to hold the string form of the GUID. If uniqueness/generation logic (NEWID()) is relied on, re-implement using UUID_STRING().

IMAGE.review: IMAGE is deprecated in SQL Server. Mapped to BINARY(8388608) (Snowflake's max BINARY size); confirm actual data size requirements.

XML.review: Snowflake has no native XML type. Mapped to VARIANT; XML must be parsed/loaded as text or converted to JSON/semi-structured data at load time.

SQL_VARIANT.review: SQL_VARIANT (mixed runtime type) has no direct Snowflake equivalent. Mapped to VARIANT; validate that all historical values convert cleanly.

GEOGRAPHY.review: Snowflake GEOGRAPHY uses WGS84/GeoJSON semantics which differ from SQL Server's GEOGRAPHY type (SRID handling, methods available). Validate spatial functions used downstream.

GEOMETRY.review: Snowflake GEOMETRY semantics differ from SQL Server GEOMETRY (planar, SRID handling, methods available). Validate spatial functions used downstream.

HIERARCHYID.review: HIERARCHYID has no Snowflake equivalent. Typically re-modeled as a path VARCHAR or an adjacency-list pattern. Manual redesign required.

ROWVERSION.review: ROWVERSION/TIMESTAMP (SQL Server auto-updating row-version column) has no Snowflake equivalent. Consider a trigger-less pattern such as a METADATA$ pseudo-column, a manually maintained UPDATED_AT TIMESTAMP, or STREAMS for change tracking.

TIMESTAMP.review: In SQL Server, a column typed TIMESTAMP (not to be confused with the SQL standard datetime meaning) is a synonym for ROWVERSION - an auto-updating binary version stamp, not a date/time value. It has no Snowflake equivalent. Confirm whether this column is actually a datetime (then it should have been DATETIME/DATETIME2) or a true rowversion column before converting.

CURSOR.review: CURSOR is not a storable column type; it cannot exist as a table column in Snowflake either. Remove or redesign.

function_mappings._comment: Applied to DEFAULT expressions and other expressions found in the DDL. Matching is case-insensitive and regex-based on the function name/pattern shown as key.

GETUTCDATE\\s*\\(\\s*\\).review: GETUTCDATE() returns UTC based on the OS clock regardless of session settings. The Snowflake replacement CONVERT_TIMEZONE('UTC', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) depends on the session TIMEZONE parameter - verify the account/session timezone is set as expected, or use SYSDATE() if the account default is already UTC.

SYSUTCDATETIME\\s*\\(\\s*\\).review: SYSUTCDATETIME() returns UTC based on the OS clock. Verify the Snowflake session TIMEZONE parameter matches expectations.

NEWID\\s*\\(\\s*\\).review: NEWID() and UUID_STRING() use different UUID generation algorithms (SQL Server: proprietary GUID; Snowflake: UUIDv4). Values will not match/collide across systems and any code relying on GUID structure/sortability (e.g. NEWSEQUENTIALID patterns) must be re-reviewed.

NEWSEQUENTIALID\\s*\\(\\s*\\).review: NEWSEQUENTIALID() produces sequential GUIDs for index-friendliness, a concept Snowflake's micro-partition storage doesn't need in the same way. Mapped to UUID_STRING(); confirm no code depends on sequential ordering of the generated ids.

SUSER_SNAME\\s*\\(\\s*\\).review: SUSER_SNAME() (current SQL Server login name) has no Snowflake equivalent. Use CURRENT_USER() if the intent is the current session's user.

bit_literal_defaults._comment: How to render DEFAULT literal values for a column whose SQL Server type was BIT (now BOOLEAN).

schema_handling._comment: Schemas in this list are SQL Server's default/system schema and are dropped, matching the worked example (dbo.Customer -> Customer). Any other schema is preserved as a Snowflake schema-qualified name (schema.table).

identifier_quoting._comment: SQL Server [bracketed] identifiers become plain identifiers in Snowflake unless they collide with a reserved word or contain characters/case that require quoting, in which case they become "double-quoted".

unsupported_table_options._comment: SQL Server clauses that are storage/engine directives with no Snowflake equivalent. Detected and stripped; each produces a manual-review note rather than being silently dropped.

patterns.reason: Filegroup placement (ON [PRIMARY]) is a SQL Server physical-storage concept. Snowflake manages physical storage automatically; the clause is removed with no functional replacement.
TEXTIMAGE_ON filegroup placement is a SQL Server physical-storage concept with no Snowflake equivalent; removed.
Table WITH(...) options (e.g. FILLFACTOR, DATA_COMPRESSION, LOCK_ESCALATION) are SQL Server storage/engine settings with no Snowflake equivalent; removed.

unsupported_column_attributes._comment: Column-level modifiers that must be flagged for manual review rather than translated, because there is no reliable automatic equivalent.

patterns.reason: ROWGUIDCOL marks a column as the row's GUID for replication features Snowflake doesn't have. Removed; re-implement replication/merge logic explicitly if needed.
PERSISTED (materialized computed column) has no Snowflake DDL equivalent. Recreate as a regular column populated by ETL, or as a view/materialized view expression.
SPARSE column storage optimization has no Snowflake equivalent (Snowflake's columnar storage already handles this automatically). Attribute removed, no action needed.
FILESTREAM (storing BLOBs on the filesystem) has no Snowflake equivalent. Store large binary objects in a stage instead and reference them by path/URL.

Dynamic Data Masking (MASKED WITH...) is a SQL Server security feature. Snowflake's equivalent is a Dynamic Data Masking policy created separately via CREATE MASKING POLICY, not inline column DDL - recreate manually.

COLLATE specifies a SQL Server collation. Snowflake collation syntax and available collations differ; review whether case-sensitivity/accent-sensitivity behavior needs to be replicated with Snowflake's COLLATE clause.

computed_column.reason: Computed column (col AS (expression)) definitions use SQL Server expression syntax and may reference functions with no Snowflake equivalent. Snowflake supports virtual/computed columns with different syntax (col TYPE AS (expression)) - the expression itself must be manually reviewed and ported, and a data type must be supplied explicitly.

constraint_notes.check: Snowflake accepts CHECK constraint syntax but does NOT enforce it (metadata only, per Snowflake documentation). If the CHECK is relied on for data integrity, enforce it in the load/ETL layer instead.
constraint_notes.foreign_key: Snowflake accepts PRIMARY KEY / FOREIGN KEY / UNIQUE constraint syntax but does NOT enforce them by default (informational/metadata only, used by the query optimizer). Application-level or ETL-level enforcement is required if referential integrity must be guaranteed.
constraint_notes.default_constraint_name: SQL Server named DEFAULT constraints (CONSTRAINT DF_x DEFAULT ...) are converted to plain Snowflake DEFAULT clauses, since Snowflake does not support naming default constraints separately.
